The largest such k is 2.

**Upper bound.** Let V be the number of vertices. Each colour class must connect all V vertices, so it has at least V−1 edges. Hence k(V−1) ≤ 2022.

A convex polyhedron has a planar graph, so E ≤ 3V−6. With E = 2022 this gives 3V ≥ 2028, so V ≥ 676. Then V−1 ≥ 675, and k ≤ 2022/675 < 3. So k ≤ 2.

**Construction for k = 2.** Take V = 1011. A 4-regular graph on 1011 vertices has 4·1011/2 = 2022 edges, and all its degrees are equal, so the degree condition holds. I did not construct or verify an explicit example. I am relying on the following: a 4-regular, 3-connected planar graph on 1011 vertices that is also 4-edge-connected should exist. By Nash-Williams' theorem, a 4-edge-connected graph has 2 edge-disjoint spanning trees. Colour one tree red, the other blue, and give each remaining edge either colour (two spanning trees use 2·1010 = 2020 of the 2022 edges). Then each colour class is connected and spanning, which gives k = 2.

ANSWER: 2
